newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Australian bonds get no help from U.S..
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Australian bonds get no help from U.S..

text.p: *Australian bond futures carried over Wednesday's negative dayside tone into the SYCOM session, weighed down further by a weak U.S. Treasury market.
*RBA's Macfarlane to testify to parliamentry committee from 10.15 a.m. (0015 GMT), April jobs data 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
Australian bond futures carried over Wednesday's negative dayside tone into the SYCOM session, weighed down further by a weak U.S. Treasury market.
The June 10-year bond futures contract ended after hours trade at 92.155 compared with Wednesday's weak pit close of 92.180 and well below this week's 92.300 high.

Failure to take out this high in initial trading on Wednesday saw a quick price reversal, and the market now risks a breakdown out of mini-rising channel which commenced in late April at 92.140, analysts said.
Further support is seen at 92.080 amd 92.030.
Meanwhile, U.S. Treasuries fell sharply after a weak response to a 10-year note refunding auction, which followed an equally soggy three-year sale on Tuesday.

Domestic bonds face too key events on Thursday with Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane due to testify to a parliamentry finance committee from around 10.15 a.m. (0015 GMT), and the April labour force report due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
The local market came under pressure from speculative, and later genuine, liquidation after the RBA's unchanged policy stance following Tuesday's board meeting.
The market is now likely to be hanging on Macfarlane's every comment in order to deduce the central bank's thinking on policy and the general economic outlook.

While Macfarlane is testifying, April labour force is expected to show a 35,000 rebound in employment after its recent poor performance, but this is not expected to have any impact on the unemployment rate, which is seen sticking at 8.7 percent, according to a Reuters survey of economists.
